title: CPU feature probe is misclassified as a user-facing CLI command
reasoning: The detected entrypoint is a NumPy distutils CPU capability probe, not a real WindieOS command. Its main() immediately executes an AVX512CD intrinsic and reads a 512-bit vector from argv memory, with no command contract, argument validation, help path, or runtime CPU guard. If clawpatch treats this as an executable CLI feature named cpu_avx512cd, invoking it on ordinary user input or an unsupported CPU can crash or fail unpredictably, and packaging/release logic may surface vendored build-check sources as product commands.
recommendation: Exclude vendored runtime paths such as frontend/python-runtime/lib/python3.11/site-packages/numpy/distutils/checks from CLI-command feature discovery, or classify these files as build probes rather than product entrypoints.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for this feature, and the file itself contains no assertions or command-level behavior to validate the claimed CLI contract.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a discovery test that scans this fixture path and asserts numpy/distutils/checks/cpu_avx512cd.c is not emitted as a cli-command feature.
minimumFixScope: Update the feature discovery classifier or ignore rules for vendored Python runtime CPU-check sources.

history.note: Excluded vendored frontend/python-runtime dependency probe from WindieOS-owned review scope
